projectDescription: A high-performance, multi-language co-simulation framework that enables multiple domain-specific simulators to exchange data and synchronize in time across scales from laptops to supercomputers.
keyFeatures: Multi-language support: C++, C, Python, Java, MATLAB, Julia, Octave, and more
Scalable from two federates on a laptop to 100,000+ on supercomputers
Distributed time synchronization across heterogeneous simulators
Value and message federate types for physics and control co-simulation
Built-in broker hierarchy for federate orchestration
Flexible configuration via JSON files, command-line, or direct API calls
Helper apps: Broker, Player, Recorder, Echo, Tracer, Clone, Connector
Docker support and package manager distributions
Used in energy domain simulations: power grid, communications, buildings, transportation
publicApiSurface: ValueFederate — publishes and subscribes to physical values
MessageFederate — sends and receives endpoint messages
CombinationFederate — combines value and message federate capabilities
CallbackFederate — event-driven federate with registered callbacks
Publications / Subscriptions / Inputs — value interface objects
Filters — message manipulation (delay, loss, clone, etc.)
Translators — convert between value and message interfaces
helicsCreateValueFederateFromConfig — create federate from JSON config
helicsCreateMessageFederateFromConfig — create message federate from JSON config
helicsCreateCombinationFederateFromConfig — create combination federate from JSON config
helics.h — unified C shared library API
